issues.description: Packetization buffer complects pacing, framing, and serialization inside the transport.
issues.detail: fixed_audio_packet_size adds a stateful chunking buffer to the transport that is only meaningful for raw PCM payloads from certain serializers. Framing is a property of the wire format (Vonage's contract), not of FastAPIWebsocketTransport. COMPLECTED: serializer-specific framing belongs in the serializer (or a small pure packetizer used by it), keeping the transport ignorant of payload shape.

issues.description: Audio send buffer is place-oriented mutable state with implicit time semantics.
issues.detail: self._audio_send_buffer is a bytearray mutated across _write_frame and process_frame (InterruptionFrame clears it). The lifetime, ownership, and ordering relative to send() are implicit. PLACE-ORIENTED: model the packetizer as a small object that takes bytes and returns a list of full chunks plus residual, so the time semantics (what was buffered, what was flushed, what was dropped on interruption) are explicit values, not in-place edits.

issues.description: Resampling, framing, and event dispatch are complected inside one serializer.
issues.detail: VonageFrameSerializer holds two resamplers as mutable identity, dispatches on isinstance, and handles DTMF/notify/connected in one method. The values (PCM bytes, sample rates, event dicts) and the effects (resample, log, decode) are braided. Decompose into a pure event parser (json -> tagged value) and a thin audio conversion function so the serializer becomes a router over data, not a method-dispatch tree.

issues.description: DTMF digit shape is guessed at runtime instead of named as data.
issues.detail: digit = message.get('digit') or message.get('dtmf', {}).get('digit') encodes uncertainty about the upstream contract as branching logic. Either the Vonage event schema says one thing or it says two; pick one based on docs and assert. INCIDENTAL-COMPLEXITY: defensive 'try both shapes' code rots into permanent ambiguity nobody dares remove.

issues.description: fixed_audio_packet_size has no pacing semantics, only size semantics.
issues.detail: The docstring example ('640 for 20ms @ 16kHz PCM16 mono') implies real-time pacing, but the code only chunks; it does not space the sends in time. If Vonage actually needs paced 20ms frames, the existing _send_interval/_next_send_time path must be wired to this buffer, otherwise bursts of buffered audio will be sent back-to-back. The PR description claims 'real-time pacing' that the diff does not deliver.

issues.description: The question that should have been asked first: whose job is wire framing.
issues.detail: Before adding fixed_audio_packet_size to a generic transport, ask: is fixed-size PCM framing a property of Vonage's protocol, or of the transport? It is Vonage's. EASY-NOT-SIMPLE: a transport flag is familiar and small, but it leaks one serializer's contract into a shared component every other serializer must now understand or ignore.

review.summary: The Vonage serializer and FastAPI transport changes work, but they complect concerns that should live in separate places. Wire-level framing (fixed-size PCM packets) is a property of the Vonage Audio Connector protocol, not of a generic WebSocket transport; pushing it into FastAPIWebsocketTransport as a flag plus a mutable bytearray makes every future serializer share a contract it does not need. The serializer itself braids resampling, event parsing, and effects in one isinstance-dispatch method. Most concerning, the PR text promises 'real-time pacing' but the diff only chunks bytes — pacing is not implemented. Recommend moving packetization into the serializer (or a small pure packetizer it composes), modeling the buffer as a value-returning function, and either delivering actual pacing or removing that claim.
